CD154-induced GM-CSF release from vascular SMC elicits monocyte adhesion and activation and thus may play a key role in the initiation and progression of atherosclerosis.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CD40/CD154 pathway is an important link between the immune system and the vasculature.
the CD40-CD154 co-stimulatory pathway is involved in atherogenesis by promoting the activation and migration of monocytes into the vessel wall, thereby enhancing the inflammatory response.
CD154-stimulated vascular SMC release proinflammatory cytokines, which activate monocytes and thus may be involved in atherogenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
vascular smooth muscle cells (vSMCs) can be activated to secrete pro-inflammatory cytokines and that the secretion of these factors is dependent on the presence of T cells.

CD40-CD154 interaction between T cells and vascular smooth muscle cells (vSMC) in the vessel wall is a novel mechanism for the activation and recruitment of monocytes to atherogenic sites, which could be targeted by therapeutic interventions.
